faqs.question: What is PRO25D used for?
faqs.answer: PRO25D is a digital homogenizer used for compounding, emulsions and suspensions, cell disruption, protein extraction, medical research, and pharmaceutical processing.

faqs.question: What is the speed range on PRO25D?
faqs.answer: Speed is precisely adjustable throughout the full 0 to 30,000 RPM range via digital control.

faqs.question: What sample volumes can PRO25D handle?
faqs.answer: It processes samples from 0.05 mL up to 3.5 L, with higher volumes dependent on viscosity.

faqs.question: What viscosity can PRO25D handle?
faqs.answer: PRO25D handles viscosity up to 50,000 mPas, suited to thick suspensions and compounds.

faqs.question: What probe sizes are compatible with PRO25D?
faqs.answer: Compatible PRO generator probes range from 5mm to 30mm in diameter.

faqs.question: Does PRO25D include a stand?
faqs.answer: Yes, a U-shape Stand Assembly is included with the unit.

faqs.question: Does PRO25D include a generator probe?
faqs.answer: No, a generator probe is required to operate the unit and is sold separately.

faqs.question: Can PRO25D handle viscous samples effectively?
faqs.answer: Yes, though viscous samples reduce maximum capacity. Adding a Deflector Head to the generator probe helps facilitate sample movement and increase max volume homogenized.

faqs.question: What is the price of PRO25D in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the probe and accessory configuration selected. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of PRO25D in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ProScientific PRO25D in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroLead: Low-viscosity and high-viscosity samples don't behave the same way under a rotor-stator, and PRO25D is built to handle both without losing precision at either end. A digital display and speed control fine-tune speed anywhere across the full 0 to 30,000 RPM range, precisely adjustable throughout, not just at fixed steps. body.text: Digital display and speed control fine-tune speed anywhere between 0 and 30,000 RPM, with precise adjustment available throughout the entire range rather than only at fixed increments.
Processing volume spans 0.05 mL up to 3.5 L, giving genuine flexibility from tiny research samples to larger lab-scale batches on the same unit.
Viscosity handling reaches up to 50,000 mPas, covering thick suspensions and compounds well beyond thin liquid samples.
Compatible PRO generator probes range from 5mm to 30mm in diameter, matched to the sample volume and viscosity being processed.
A U-shape Stand Assembly is included with the homogenizer, so no separate stand purchase is needed to get the unit running.
The unit is versatile enough for compounding, emulsions and suspensions, cell disruption, protein extractions, medical research, and pharmaceutical processing.
A generator probe is required to operate the unit and is sold separately, and viscous samples will reduce maximum processing capacity.
Adding a Deflector Head to a generator probe facilitates sample movement during homogenization and helps increase max volume homogenized.

paragraphs: Some processes need brute force at high RPM. Others need delicate control at the low end where a heavier touch would damage a sample. PRO25D is built to deliver both precisely, not just broadly.

Digital speed control allows precise adjustment throughout the entire 0 to 30,000 RPM range, rather than snapping between fixed speed steps that might overshoot what a sensitive sample or delicate emulsion actually needs. That level of control matters directly for protocols like cell disruption or protein extraction, where consistency between runs depends on hitting the exact same speed every time, not an approximate one.
sections.note: Tell our team the RPM range your protocols typically operate in, and Inkarp will confirm the right probe and setup for that range.

sections.title: High-Viscosity Processing
body: How PRO25D handles samples up to 50,000 mPas without losing performance.
Thick, viscous samples push most rotor-stator homogenizers to their limits, and that's exactly where PRO25D's 50,000 mPas rating earns its place.

Viscosity handling up to 50,000 mPas means compounds, thick suspensions, and dense formulations process on the same unit that handles thin liquid samples, without needing separate equipment for each viscosity range. That capability, combined with generator probes ranging from 5mm to 30mm in diameter, lets the probe itself be matched to how thick and how large the sample actually is. Where viscosity does reduce maximum processing capacity, adding a Deflector Head to the generator probe helps move sample material more effectively, increasing the maximum volume that can still be homogenized.
